? Intrinsic innervation: which corresponds to the cardioneuron system, responsible for cardiac automatism. ? Extrinsic innervation: which ensures the nervous regulation of cardiac automatism and which is ensured by two systems: - the sympathetic, cardio-accelerator system. - the parasympathetic system, cardio-brake. These two sympathetic and parasympathetic systems give rise to the cardiac nerves, which form cardiac plexuses (or branches).

headers: has. The parasympathetic system: It is formed by the branches of the vagus nerve, schematically distributed on each side into three:
rows: ? Superior cardiac nerve, arising from the trunk of the vagus nerve, downstream of the inferior ganglion of the vagus nerve, ? Middle cardiac nerve, arising from the loop of the recurrent laryngeal nerve. ? Lower cardiac nerve, originating below the loop of the recurrent laryngeal nerve. b. The sympathetic system: It is formed by the branches born from the lymph nodes of the cervical chain, distributed, on each side, into three groups:

? Superior cardiac nerve, arising from the superior cervical ganglion. ? Middle cardiac nerve, largest branch, arising from the middle cervical ganglion. ? Lower cardiac nerve, very short, arises from the lower cervical ganglion (cervico-thoracic ganglion or subclavian loop. c. Cardiac plexuses: All the nerves of the heart resolve into two plexuses:

? The anterior arterial plexus (or superior cardiac plexus): It surrounds the ascending aorta and the pulmonary artery, with the Wrisberg ganglion located under the horizontal part of the aortic arch. It brings together nerve threads from:

- From the cardiac nerves of the two sympathetic nerves, - From the left vagus, and from the superior contingent of the right vagus. From this plexus arise the right and left coronary plexuses from which the subpericardial and subendocardial plexuses arise.

? The posterior venous plexus (or lower cardiac plexus): It surrounds the pulmonary veins and the superior vena cava. It brings together nerve threads coming from: - Cardiac nerves of the right sympathetic nerve, - Lower and middle contingents of the right vagus nerve. They give rise to the atrial nerves which form the atrial plexus

blocks.text: III. INTRINSIC INNERVATION: cardionector system The cardionector system is responsible for coordinating the contractions of the different cardiac cavities. It is made up of formations in clusters (sino-atrial node and atrio-ventricular node), and of fibers united in bundles (atrio-ventricular bundle) and their branches.
has. Sino-atrial node (Keith and Flack node): It projects under the epicardium, on the right atrium near the junction of the superior vena cava.

b. Atrioventricular node (Aschoff-Tawara node): It is located under the endocardium of the lower part of the inter-atrial septum. It is anteromedial to the ostium of the coronary sinus. It is vascularized by the branches of the right coronary artery.
c. Internodal bundles: These are pathways that unite the sinuatrial node and the atrioventricular node, we distinguish:

- An anterior bundle, which passes through the upper edge of the inter-atrial septum, - An intermediate bundle, goes around the upper edge of the fossa ovalis, - A posterior bundle, which runs along the terminal crest to pass in front or behind the ostium of the coronary sinus. d. Atrioventricular bundles (His bundle): It extends the atrioventricular node, it travels in the atrioventricular septum and the interventricular septum. It is made up of a trunk which is divided into two branches, right and left, intended for each ventricle. The right branch runs through the interventricular septum, then the septo-marginal trabecula and ends under the endocardium in a Purkinje network. The left branch travels through the interventricular septum to reach the left ventricle. It ends under the endocardium in a Purkinje network. Summary Innervation Extrinsic innervation regulates cardiac automatism and is provided by two systems: The parasympathetic system: Formed by branches of the vagus nerve, with three nerves on each side: the cardiac nerves (superior, middle, inferior).

The anterior arterial plexus (or superior cardiac plexus): Consists of nerve fibers from the cardiac nerves of both sympathetic chains, the left vagus nerve, and the upper contingent of the right vagus nerve. It condenses into the ganglion of Wrisberg. The posterior venous plexus (or inferior cardiac plexus): Includes nerve fibers from the cardiac nerves of the right sympathetic chain and the lower and middle contingents of the right vagus nerve. It provides two types of fibers: right fibers descending behind the right atrium and left fibers descending along the posterior aspect of the ventricles.
